question: How are the steering arms set to achieve the Ackerman angle?

options.text: At right angle to spindle body

solution:
The correct answer is __Slanted towards vehicle centre.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ackerman steering geometry__ is designed to prevent tire slippage while cornering.
 
• It ensures that all wheels of the vehicle follow concentric circular paths during a turn.
 
• The steering arms are angled towards the vehicle centre to achieve this effect.
 
• This geometry is based on trapezoidal linkage design principles.
 
• Proper Ackerman geometry enhances cornering performance and reduces tire wear.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Wheel Alignment:**

 
 
• Proper wheel alignment is critical for vehicle stability and tire longevity.
 
• It involves adjusting the angles of the wheels so they are perpendicular to the ground and parallel to each other.
 
 
 
• **Types of Steering Mechanisms:**
 
 
• There are two main types of steering mechanisms: Rack and Pinion, and Recirculating Ball.
 
• Both systems aim to provide precise control over the steering angle of the wheels.
 
 
 
• **Understeer and Oversteer:**
 
 
• Understeer occurs when the front wheels lose grip, causing the vehicle to turn less than intended.
 
• Oversteer occurs when the rear wheels lose grip, causing the vehicle to turn more than intended.
